To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the corneal permeability of natural prostaglanding is poor, 2) the ester prodruggs of PGF2 alpha showed higher corneall permeability than PGF2 alpha and 3) all compounds tested showed good sclearal permeability.
the corneoscleral permeability of prostaglandins, their ester pro-drugs and analogs were measured using human cornea and/or sclera in vitro.
natural PGs, PGF2alpha ester prodrags and PG analogs have poor corneal permeabilities and good scleral permeabilities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ocular penetration of PGs and their prodrugs, which are potential therapeutic agents for ocular diseases.
the ocular pharmacokinetics of PGF2 alpha and its ester prodrug and analogs.
the development of a novel approach to the design of prodrugs of prostaglandins with the aim of increasing their bioavailability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PGs and their analogs are not likely to be effective ocular hypotensive agents due to their poor corneal permeabilities, but the PG ester prodrags may be promising candidates for the treatment of glaucoma.
the cornea is a major rate-limiting barrier for the ocular absorption, while the sclera is a major facilitator for ocular drug penetration.
the PGF2 alpha prodrugs are more permeable than PGF2 alpha and the analogues are more permeable in the sclera but less permeable in the cornea.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PGF2alpha ester prodrug (e.g. 11-pivalate) is a better candidate than PGF2α for topical ocular therapy.
the PGs and ester prodrug derivatives have low corneal permeability and high scleral permeability.
the ester prodrug of PGF2-alpha, 11,15-Dipivaloyl-PGF2-alpha, is a good candidate for ocular drug delivery, because of its high transcleral penetration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ester prodrug 11-pivalate PGF(2alpha) is a potential prodrug for ocular delivery of PGF(2)alpha.
ester prodrug approaches are promising for improving ocular absorption of PGF2 alpha.
the cornea is a significant barrier to ocular penetration for PGs and their prodrugs.
